BudgetWise is an ASP.NET Core Web API with a React/TypeScript frontend; .NET 8, Vite, Tailwind CSS. Training app for the GitHub Copilot Workshop.

**Code:** Follow C# naming conventions (PascalCase types/methods/properties; camelCase locals/parameters); use meaningful names, focused methods, composition, C# 12 where appropriate, `var` when type is obvious, and `using` inside namespaces. Use strict TypeScript; React hooks and functional components; focused, reusable components; Tailwind classes, semantic HTML, accessibility, and no inline styles. Use constructor dependency injection and appropriate service lifetimes; consistently use minimal APIs or controllers. Keep code clear, simple, beginner-friendly, and demonstrate best practices.

**Backend/API:** RESTful plural resource nouns, appropriate HTTP methods/status codes, IDs in path variables, filters in query parameters, camelCase JSON, and proper Content-Type headers. Return `IActionResult` or typed results; validate inputs with Data Annotations or FluentValidation and return meaningful errors. Use DTOs for payloads, immutable DTO `record` types, explicit domain/DTO mapping, and validation annotations. Use built-in middleware where appropriate. Use nullable reference types and `required` for mandatory properties; initialize models with properties and add navigation properties for related entities.

**Docs/comments:** Add XML documentation to all public classes and methods, including `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, and `<exception>` where applicable; add TypeScript JSDoc. Explain WHY, not just WHAT. Mark incomplete features with `// TODO:` and a clear description; preserve workshop TODOs and follow existing patterns when implementing them. Explain .NET Core and React concepts.

**Data:** Use in-memory collections for development/testing. Populate realistic representative sample data via `MockData` class in `Data/MockData.cs`; use thread-safe collections where necessary.

**Tests:** Use xUnit and React Testing Library; AAA (Arrange, Act, Assert); descriptive names `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`; `WebApplicationFactory<T>` for integration tests; mock external dependencies and API calls with MSW or similar. Cover success, failure, edge/boundary cases, accessibility, and user interactions (not implementation details); use Testing Library `screen` queries. Write tests for new features.

**Workflow:** Check similar project code first; follow ASP.NET and existing frontend patterns; include error handling and validation; write tests alongside implementation; document features; use backend Data Annotations and frontend form validation; ensure frontend/backend coherence.

❌ Do not use service locator pattern (always use dependency injection)
❌ Do not return null from API endpoints (use `NotFound()` or throw exceptions)
❌ Do not put business logic in controllers (use services)
❌ Do not ignore exceptions or use empty catch blocks
❌ Do not use `any` type in TypeScript (use proper types or `unknown`)
❌ Do not create side effects in React component render functions

**Commands:**
```sh
cd budgetwise-app/backend
dotnet restore              # Restore dependencies
dotnet build                # Build the project
dotnet run                  # Start the API server (port 5000)
dotnet test                 # Run tests
dotnet watch run            # Run with hot reload
cd budgetwise-app/frontend
npm install                 # Install dependencies
npm run dev                 # Start dev server with Vite (port 5173)
npm run build               # Production build
npm run preview             # Preview production build
npm run lint                # Run ESLint
npm run test                # Run tests
```

**Project paths:**
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Program.cs` - Entry point and middleware
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Controllers/` - REST endpoints
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Models/` - Domain models and DTOs
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Services/` - Business logic
- `budgetwise-app/backend/Data/MockData.cs`
